items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: I was always told that if you learned how to read music... But we'd say 'no man, I don't want to be mechanical'... Well he came in and asked... I say 'yeah, what the hell, yeah, come up and play a couple of tunes.'... We just backed him up, let him play all he wanted

ctx.x: Yeah, I met Charlie Parker through that same sittin' in process. Very few people like it when you got your own group and you all been playing every night and you get your set routines and things. When somebody sits in that automatically makes it a jam session. But this particular night this fellow came in, I had never seen him before...
Charlie Parker? before we get into that I wanted to ask you if people sat in much with the Tatum trio.

No, there really wasn't no takers, in a way of speaking. Because they knew if they got in there, he didn't play around. I said, the only fellow that ever sat in with us that I know of was Buddy Rich. He played drums. There was no other -- I don't even remember Oscar Moore sittin' in. And he was one of the greatest guitar players around at that particular time. But he was with the King Cole trio.
